question: How do I pay a parking citation?
expected_answer: Pay online with the citation number or your license plate and state; don't pay if you plan to contest it, since paying admits liability and closes the dispute window.

question: Can I park my RV on the street overnight in Pacific Beach?
expected_answer: Not by default -- oversized vehicles over 27 ft long and 7 ft tall can't park on the street 2-6 a.m. under the Neighborhood Parking Protection Ordinance; a Temporary Overnight RV Permit (about $1.50/24 hours) is the legal way to do it.

question: How do I get a residential parking permit for my street?
expected_answer: Apply online if your address is in an established residential permit district; the annual permit is about $11.50 (estimate) and most addresses can hold up to four permits.

question: Will I get a ticket for parking on the street during street sweeping?
expected_answer: Only if your block has a posted 'no parking' sign with the sweeping day/time -- most swept blocks in the City don't have a sign and aren't ticketed for sweeping itself; check the street sweeping map for your address.

question: How do I start water service at my new apartment?
expected_answer: Submit a request online at water.sandiego.gov/s/movein or call 619-515-3500; it can take up to 10 business days to process.

question: I have a leak outside near the street -- is that my responsibility?
expected_answer: A leak on the City's side of the meter (typically the street-facing side) should be reported to the 24/7 Water and Sewer Emergency Line at 619-515-3525; a leak on your side of the meter is the owner's responsibility.

question: Is my trash fee included on my water bill?
expected_answer: No -- the residential trash fee from Measure B is billed through the county property tax bill, not through MyWaterSD.

question: What do I need to license a short-term rental / Airbnb in San Diego?
expected_answer: A Short-Term Residential Occupancy (STRO) license from the City Treasurer in one of four tiers based on days rented per year and whether the host lives on-site, plus a TOT certificate and Rental Unit Business Tax certificate.

question: How big can an ADU be and do I need a permit for it?
expected_answer: Up to 1,200 sq ft (no cap for a conversion of an existing structure), minimum 150 sq ft; a Building Permit is always required, there's no exemption.

question: My landlord wants to raise my rent a lot next month, is there a limit?
expected_answer: California's statewide rent cap generally limits most increases to 5% plus local inflation or 10%, whichever is lower, with 30 or 90 days' notice depending on the size of the increase; for a dispute, the City refers residents to the Legal Aid Society of San Diego.

question: Who do I call if I'm about to lose my housing and need help tonight?
expected_answer: Call the San Diego Housing Commission's HOUSING FIRST -- SAN DIEGO hotline at 619-578-7768.

question: How do I report a car that's been sitting on my street for weeks without moving?
expected_answer: A vehicle parked more than 72 consecutive hours without being driven at least a tenth of a mile counts as abandoned; report it online through Get It Done or call SDPD's Vehicle Abatement Unit.
